newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slumbers, heating barge spreads ease.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slumbers, heating barge spreads ease.

text.p: European gas oil physical trade barely left the starting gate on Friday with heating oil and diesel traders engaging in very little substantial discussion.
Outright values crept 25 cents high. August IPE was trading at $169.50 a tonne, September 50 cents higher at $171 a tonne.
Heating oil barges traded easier. A prompt 1,000 tonne barge moved 25 cents down at August IPE +$0.25 fob ARA. A 1,250 tonne parcel also changed hands for the same premium and period.
Low sulphur diesel was notionally assessed at Aug IPE +3.75/$4.25, little changed.
Demand for gas oil was again curbed by the strong dollar, which was trading at 1.8466/71 marks at 1142 GMT. It touched a seven year high on Monday of 1.8490 marks.
Two large cargoes of Russian heating were heard traded into ARA, one done at a 75 discount to September IPE cif NWE and the other at a 75 cent premium to mean of the means cif NWE.
Diesel cargoes were notionally assessed at $5.25 above August IPE, and bid at $4.50.
Cargo activity has shrunk with the absence of key traders on holiday, lack of arbitrage opportunities to South America or the Far East and the high dollar.
